title: Pasta 'Ncasciata Siciliana
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A festive baked pasta from Messina, layers of short pasta packed with meatballs, eggplant, salami, hard-boiled eggs, and two cheeses, pressed and baked until it holds together like a cake.
longDesc: Pasta 'ncasciata means 'boxed' or 'encased' pasta, reflecting how the dish is tightly packed into its baking pan before cooking, resulting in a dense, richly layered casserole that slices cleanly like a savory cake once cooled slightly.
ingredients: 500 g (1.1 lb) short pasta such as maccheroni or rigatoni
200 g (2 cups) caciocavallo or provolone, diced
steps: Prepare the fried eggplant, browned meatballs, and tomato sauce ahead of assembling.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until very al dente, a couple of minutes less than usual.
Drain the pasta and toss with about half the tomato sauce.
Oil a deep round baking pan and line with a layer of fried eggplant slices, letting some hang over the edge.
Layer in a portion of pasta, followed by meatballs, salami, sliced egg, diced cheese, and a little more sauce.
Repeat the layers, finishing with pasta and a final layer of eggplant, folding the overhanging slices over the top to enclose everything.
Press down gently and top with the remaining sauce and pecorino.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 35–40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Let rest for 15 minutes before inverting onto a plate or slicing directly from the pan.
chefTips: Undercooking the pasta slightly before assembling is important, as it continues cooking in the oven.
Lining the pan with eggplant slices that overhang the edges allows you to fold them over the top, fully enclosing the filling.
Letting the dish rest before slicing helps it hold together in clean pieces.
commonMistakes: Overcooking the pasta before assembling, resulting in a mushy final texture.
Skipping the resting time, causing the layers to fall apart when sliced.
Under-seasoning any individual layer, which can leave parts of the dish tasting flat.
reheating: Reheat covered in the oven until warmed through.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the meat and eggs.
culturalNote: Pasta 'ncasciata is a festive specialty of Messina, traditionally prepared for special occasions given the effort its many layered components require.
